# FactLot

> FactLot is an open-source fact layer for commercial real estate (CRE) AI agents. It gives an agent 26 deterministic calculators (rent schedule, net effective rent, proposal comparison, percentage rent, CAM reconciliation, debt sizing, ASC 842 remeasurement, prepayment and defeasance, WALT, NPV, IRR, lease vs. own, renew vs. relocate, hotel metrics, property DCF pro forma, direct capitalization, loan amortization schedules, LP/GP equity waterfalls, 1031 exchange deadlines and boot, multifamily rent rolls, capital expenditure recovery, building-wide CAM reconciliation, lease critical dates, the Texas unequal-appraisal arithmetic, and tie-outs of a DCF or CAM reconciliation against another system's export) that return the value, every step, warnings, and a versioned formula ID; FactLot IDs for parcels, legal entities, buildings (from the street address), suites, and documents that any agent can compute offline, and minted IDs for leases; and a fact model in which every claim carries its source citation and AI-use rights.

Use FactLot when a task needs lease, rent, CAM, loan, or return arithmetic with an audit trail; a stable ID to join a parcel, owner, suite, or document across systems; a validated, cited fact to store or share; or a check that what an agent read from a lease is actually in it. It does not cover everything: beyond parcels and owners, the project's registry holds zoning, recorded sales, deeds and mortgages, energy benchmarks and CMBS loan data only for some metros (see the coverage page), and today only the DC sample and the GSA lease comps are downloadable. The hosted API answers registry lookups for the places the "Hosted registry" paragraph below lists (call `registry_coverage` first; see the registry documentation below).

Use the document tools when an agent reads a lease, amendment, estoppel or rent roll: extract each term with its verbatim quote and page, then call `doc_verify_facts` (FactLot checks deterministically that the quote is on that page and states the value, and returns cited facts, review items and rejections with reasons), `doc_abstract_lease` (current-state abstract with amendment precedence), `doc_compare` (estoppel or rent roll vs the lease) or `doc_verify_claim`. No model runs on FactLot's side, nothing is stored, and the checks are textual: they do not find terms the agent missed. Guide: https://github.com/9mp96ygnbk-alt/factlot/blob/main/docs/document-verification.md

Proof: Excel workbooks reconciling every calculator to live spreadsheet formulas at zero difference: https://github.com/9mp96ygnbk-alt/factlot/tree/main/examples/reconciliation ; registry coverage by county: https://github.com/9mp96ygnbk-alt/factlot/blob/main/docs/registry/coverage.md ; licence and AI-use rights per source: https://github.com/9mp96ygnbk-alt/factlot/blob/main/docs/registry/rights.md

Also: `doc_spread_statement` (T-12 or operating statement onto a published chart of accounts, every line cited, totals footed), `doc_check_use_conflict` (a proposed use against verified exclusives and prohibited uses; potential conflicts for human review), `fact_package_create`/`fact_package_verify` (hash-chained fact packages, optionally signed with your own Ed25519 key), and `lease_comp_validate` (validate a shared lease comp and derive its net effective rent). `doc_predicates` lists every lease predicate's value shape, an example, and which parts are checked against the quote; a person's confirmation (`confirmation: {by, at}`) turns a value no quote can prove (a go-dark covenant, a CAM cap method) into a `human_verified` fact, and rent tables written by lease year verify with dates derived from a cited commencement date. `calc_reconcile_dcf` and `calc_reconcile_cam` compare FactLot with an ARGUS, Yardi or other export line by line and name likely convention causes as hypotheses (tested on synthetic exports only; parity with ARGUS or Yardi is untested). Agent frameworks (LangGraph/LangChain, OpenAI Agents SDK, CrewAI, MCP Python/TypeScript SDKs, Vercel AI SDK): tested recipes at https://github.com/9mp96ygnbk-alt/factlot/blob/main/connectors/frameworks/README.md Draft rules packs (NYC LL97, Washington Clean Buildings, Boston BERDO) are in the SDKs for review only: not verified, not served as tools.

Lease comps, free: search them on the hosted API with `lease_comp_search` (filters by state, county, city, ZIP, radius, size, dates and rent, with summary statistics and a citation on every answer), or download https://github.com/9mp96ygnbk-alt/factlot/releases/download/lease-comps-gsa-2026-11-04/factlot-lease-comps-gsa-2026-11-04.db.gz (5.3 MB, public domain; 6,994 federal GSA lease comps with rent per RSF, area, dates and building IDs; government-tenant leases, not market comps for every use) and set FACTLOT_REGISTRY_DB to it; share your own comps in the same format with `lease_comp_validate` (https://github.com/9mp96ygnbk-alt/factlot/blob/main/docs/lease-comps.md).

Fastest path, nothing to install: connect any MCP client to the hosted remote MCP server at https://api.factlot.com/mcp (Streamable HTTP, stateless). The free tier needs no key and allows 60 requests a minute per address. REST and OpenAPI are at https://api.factlot.com/openapi.json (OpenAPI 3.1, every tool; /openapi-3.0.json is the curated subset of at most 30 operations for Custom GPT Actions, and /openapi-3.0.json?operations=all gives every tool in 3.0), and https://api.factlot.com/ describes the endpoints and plans as JSON. For Claude Code: `claude mcp add --transport http factlot https://api.factlot.com/mcp`. Or install the FactLot Claude Code plugin, which adds twelve CRE skills (loan sizing and amortization, lease economics, CAM reconciliation, ASC 842, lease vs own and renewals, investment returns, valuation, 1031 exchanges, multifamily rent rolls, hotel metrics, Texas protest deadline, Texas unequal-appraisal arithmetic) wired to these tools: `/plugin marketplace add 9mp96ygnbk-alt/factlot`, then `/plugin install factlot@factlot`.

Claude (Desktop, claude.ai, mobile) custom connectors and ChatGPT developer-mode apps cannot send a key header: add the connector https://api.factlot.com/mcp/signin and sign in with OAuth 2.1 (paste a Pro or Team key once on the FactLot sign-in page, or continue on the free tier). Without credentials /mcp/signin answers 401 with `WWW-Authenticate` naming https://api.factlot.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp; bare /mcp stays open on the free tier.

Plans (every tool is on every plan, except three things for Pro and Team only: the two model-backed tools below, the full multi-year value history from `registry_get`, and the batch lookup `registry_tx_equity_candidates_batch`): Free, no key: every calculator, ID, fact, rules and document tool at 60 requests a minute per IP address, 25 registry lookups a day per IP address, and 3 reports a month per IP address; `registry_get` returns the current roll year only in `value_history` and `history` (the answer says what was left out and links https://factlot.com/pricing/), and `registry_tx_equity_candidates_batch` answers PlanRequired with that link and counts nothing (`registry_tx_equity_candidates`, one parcel per call, stays within the free lookups and its subject carries the value history by tax year for Pro and Team, the current roll year only on the free tier, the candidates being the same; the calculator and rules batch tools stay free). Pro, $49 a month or $490 a year (checkout `interval=year`; same limits): 1 API key, 600 requests a minute, 5,000 registry lookups a month, 50 reports a month, full value history, the registry batch lookup, email support. Team, $599 a month: up to 5 API keys, 3,000 requests a minute, 100,000 registry lookups a month, 1,000 reports a month, full value history, the registry batch lookup, priority support, and a vote on which regions open next. Limits are hard caps with no overage charges: at a cap the call returns HTTP 429 with the reset time and a link to https://factlot.com/pricing/. A lookup is one answered call to a `registry_` tool. `registry_coverage`, coverage misses (a county or system that is not loaded) and input errors are not counted; `registry_tx_equity_candidates_batch` counts one per answered subject. Free lookups count per IP address per day, paid lookups per subscription per month (shared by a plan's keys), and calculator, ID, fact, rules and document tools never count. Paid plans renew until cancelled (monthly, or yearly on Pro yearly); cancel any time at https://factlot.com/account, in the Stripe billing portal, or by email to contact@factlot.com with the subject "Cancel" from your account email. Registry download licence: $2,400 a year per state file, refreshed weekly, for internal use (not redistribution), available on request at contact@factlot.com. Enterprise (private deployment, invoicing, a signed data-processing agreement with a no-training commitment, and SSO): by quote. An agent can start checkout with `POST https://api.factlot.com/v1/billing/checkout` and body `{"plan":"pro"}` (add `"interval":"year"` for Pro yearly); it returns a Stripe link for the human to pay, and the API key is shown once on the page Stripe returns to and can take up to a minute to start working. Send the key as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. Plans as JSON: https://api.factlot.com/v1/plans. Terms: https://factlot.com/terms. Privacy: https://factlot.com/privacy

Model-backed tools (hosted only, Pro and Team keys, listed only while the operator has configured a model; otherwise 503 `ModelUnavailable`): `doc_extract_lease` (`POST /v1/doc/extract_lease`; a model reads a lease and FactLot keeps only values it verifies verbatim on the cited page; 100 pages a month on Pro, 2,000 on Team) and `report_narrative` (`POST /v1/report/narrative`; prose drafted from one FactLot result, every figure verified against it; 50 a month on Pro, 1,000 on Team). These two, and only these, send what you submit to Anthropic's API; every other tool runs without a model. Without a key they answer 403 `PlanRequired`.

Reports (hosted only, every plan): `report_create` (`POST /v1/reports`) builds an XLSX workbook, PDF or ICS calendar from a FactLot tool result, by code with no model. Eight kinds: `tx_unequal_appraisal`, `lease_abstract`, `cam_reconciliation`, `debt_sizing`, `asc842_schedule`, `compare_proposals`, `dcf_summary`, `critical_dates`. Send the tool's `arguments`; FactLot runs the tool and prints its figures. The answer is a download link that works 24 hours, after which the file is deleted. 3 a month free per IP address, 50 on Pro, 1,000 on Team; reports never count as registry lookups. See https://github.com/9mp96ygnbk-alt/factlot/blob/main/docs/reports.md

Reports (hosted, every plan): `report_create` over MCP or `POST https://api.factlot.com/v1/reports` turns a FactLot result into a client-ready XLSX, PDF or ICS file, built by code with no model, and returns a download link that works 24 hours; 3 reports a month free per IP address, 50 on Pro, 1,000 on Team. Docs: https://github.com/9mp96ygnbk-alt/factlot/blob/main/docs/reports.md

Or run it yourself from GitHub. The packages are not yet on npm or PyPI. The local MCP server needs Node.js 22.6 or newer, no API key, and makes no network calls:

```
git clone https://github.com/9mp96ygnbk-alt/factlot.git && cd factlot
npm install && npm run build
claude mcp add factlot -- node "$PWD/packages/mcp/dist/bin.js"
```

Or, with no clone, run the release build as a stdio server: `npx -y https://github.com/9mp96ygnbk-alt/factlot/releases/download/v0.5.0/factlot-mcp-standalone-0.5.0.tgz` (for Claude Code: `claude mcp add factlot -- npx -y <that URL>`). For any other MCP client, run `node packages/mcp/dist/bin.js` as a stdio server. For Python: `pip install "git+https://github.com/9mp96ygnbk-alt/factlot.git#subdirectory=python"`, then use `factlot.anthropic_tools()`, `factlot.openai_tools()`, and `factlot.run_tool(name, input)`. For REST, OpenAPI, and remote MCP: `docker build -t factlot . && docker run -p 8787:8787 factlot`. Licenses: Apache-2.0 and MIT.

When reporting a number from a calculator, cite its formula ID (for example `calc.cam_reconciliation@2`) and the returned `steps`, and surface every returned `warnings` entry to a human.

Hosted registry: the hosted API answers the `registry_*` tools for Maryland (all 24 jurisdictions; 109,249 commercial parcels and 2,812 buildings from SDAT data as of 2026-11-05, public domain), the District of Columbia (18,077 commercial parcels, 5,513 registered business entities and 396 buildings, with owners of record that are organisations, zoning and recorded sales; CC BY 4.0), Juab and Summit counties in Utah (1,528 parcels, snapshot as of 2025-11-26; CC BY 4.0, "State of Utah, SGID"), sixteen Texas counties (305,684 commercial parcels: Harris 87,717 with 3,511 buildings, Dallas 59,645 with 998 buildings, Travis 30,556 with 407 buildings, Collin 18,035 with 656 buildings, Denton 13,304 with 311 buildings, Williamson 11,758 with 402 buildings, Cameron 14,173 with 98 buildings, Nueces 13,634 with 493 buildings, Galveston 10,088 with 274 buildings, Jefferson 9,594 with 204 buildings, Brazos 8,252 with 64 buildings, Midland 7,641, Ector 7,036, Grayson 6,613 with 41 buildings, Guadalupe 4,081 with 33 buildings and Kaufman 3,557 with 42 buildings; Denton and Williamson from 2027 preliminary rolls as of 2026-11-07; several counties hold more than one roll year (Brazos 2016 to 2026, Nueces 2021 to 2026, Galveston 2023 to 2026, Kaufman 2024 to 2026, Jefferson and Guadalupe 2025 to 2026); Midland has no values because its publisher's file has none; value history by tax year, organisation owners only, and the 88,176 Texas Comptroller entities that own a hosted parcel; `registry_tx_equity_candidates` and its batch form answer for these counties; appraisal-district rolls are public record with no licence stated, cited per fact with each source's rights), New York City (all five boroughs; 164,633 commercial parcels and 5,071 buildings from the Department of Finance final assessment roll as of 2026-05-15, public record with no restrictions on use, with owners of record that are organisations, and the 66,510 New York Department of State entities that own a hosted parcel), Los Angeles County (203,179 commercial parcels from the Assessor's parcel data roll as of 2026-10-14; no owner names, which the public file does not carry; the County's open-data terms allow commercial use), San Francisco (19,048 commercial parcels from the Assessor's secured roll (the 2025 roll year, the latest published; file as of 2026-06-26); no owner names, which the public file does not carry; public domain (PDDL)), the City of Boston (the City of Boston only, not Chelsea, Revere or Winthrop, the rest of Suffolk County; 13,296 commercial parcels from the Assessing Department's fiscal-year 2026 file, with values as of 2025-01-01, older than the other regions; public domain (ODC-PDDL)), Denver (13,539 commercial parcels from the Assessor's file as of 2026-10-29; CC BY 3.0, "City and County of Denver", and the 6,678 Colorado Secretary of State entities that own a hosted parcel) and Connecticut (43,398 commercial parcels in eight former counties, from the towns' grand lists in the statewide parcel and CAMA layer as of 2026-11-09; CC0, and the 23,752 Connecticut Secretary of the State entities that own a hosted parcel): 891,631 parcels in 60 counties, on every plan including the free tier (25 lookups a day per IP address). Call `registry_coverage` first to see exactly what is hosted. Every answer cites its source file and licence or attribution. Other regions in the project's pipeline run only on a self-hosted FactLot with a registry file; more hosted regions open as their terms allow. Tarrant County is not served by the hosted registry while the publisher's terms for AI use are unclear.

Registry sample on real data: download https://github.com/9mp96ygnbk-alt/factlot/releases/download/registry-sample-dc-2026-11-07/factlot-registry-sample-dc-2026-11-07.db.gz (23.5 MB, CC BY 4.0; 18,077 District of Columbia commercial parcels, 5,513 owning entities, 7,931 cited ownership links, 396 buildings, zoning for 16,648 parcels and the latest sale for 12,594), gunzip it, and set `FACTLOT_REGISTRY_DB` to its path when starting the MCP server to run the nine `registry_*` tools on your own machine.

Further hosted registry regions, enterprise terms, and private deployments: email contact@factlot.com.

## Use it

- [Try a lookup](https://factlot.com/try/): look up a commercial property by address on the hosted free tier, with no key, and see the cited record and the raw JSON an agent receives
- [Hosted MCP server](https://factlot.com/mcp-server/): hosted remote MCP at `https://api.factlot.com/mcp`, no key; per-client setup for Claude, Claude Code, ChatGPT, Cursor, VS Code, Gemini CLI and agent frameworks
- [Connect](https://factlot.com/connect/): one page per surface (Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot Studio, Bedrock, Cursor, VS Code, Windsurf, Zed, agent frameworks) with the URL, command or config to paste; the same information as JSON at https://factlot.com/connect.json
- [Calculators](https://factlot.com/calculators/): every calculator, with worked examples and audit trails for net effective rent, debt sizing, CAM, yield maintenance, ASC 842, WALT, direct cap and equity waterfalls
- [Texas property tax protest deadline](https://factlot.com/texas/property-tax-protest-deadline/): the next three seasons' deadlines with statute citations
- [Connectors](https://github.com/9mp96ygnbk-alt/factlot/blob/main/connectors/README.md): remote MCP at `https://api.factlot.com/mcp` and REST/OpenAPI at `/v1` and `/openapi.json`, with setup for Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot, Bedrock, and others
- [MCP server](https://github.com/9mp96ygnbk-alt/factlot/blob/main/packages/mcp/README.md): `npx -y https://github.com/9mp96ygnbk-alt/factlot/releases/download/v0.5.0/factlot-mcp-standalone-0.5.0.tgz` (or `npx -y @factlot/mcp` after first publish to npm), with tools `calc_*`, `id_*`, `rules_*`, `fact_validate`, `search`, `fetch`, and `schema_get` (`report_create` is hosted only)
- [Python SDK](https://github.com/9mp96ygnbk-alt/factlot/blob/main/python/README.md): `factlot.anthropic_tools()`, `factlot.openai_tools()`, `factlot.run_tool(name, input)`
- [Agent guide](https://github.com/9mp96ygnbk-alt/factlot/blob/main/docs/agents.md): which tool to call when, how to map lease language to inputs, and how to emit cited facts

## Reference

- [Tool definitions (JSON Schema)](https://github.com/9mp96ygnbk-alt/factlot/blob/main/spec/schemas/tools.json): every calculator's input schema, with field descriptions
- [Fact model](https://github.com/9mp96ygnbk-alt/factlot/blob/main/docs/fact-model.md): facts, provenance, rights, and supersession
- [FactLot ID spec](https://github.com/9mp96ygnbk-alt/factlot/blob/main/docs/id-spec.md): URN and short-ID formats and normalization rules
- [Registry and source catalog](https://github.com/9mp96ygnbk-alt/factlot/blob/main/docs/registry/sources/README.md): 40 verified public-record sources, 1,733,923 commercial parcels in 330 counties (19 states and DC) built in the project's pipeline, and 14.2 million registered entities (queryable today on the hosted API: Maryland, the District of Columbia, Juab and Summit counties in Utah, and Harris, Dallas, Travis, Collin, Denton and Williamson counties in Texas; every other region needs a self-hosted FactLot with a registry file), with the licence and AI-use status of each source
- [Conformance vectors](https://github.com/9mp96ygnbk-alt/factlot/blob/main/spec/README.md): shared test cases every SDK must pass
- Trust: [status](https://factlot.com/status/) (live health endpoint, incident history), [security](https://factlot.com/security/) (what is stored, keys, disclosure, no SOC 2 yet), [service levels](https://factlot.com/sla/) (no SLA today, draft terms, versioning), [assurance](https://factlot.com/assurance/) (how the numbers are proven and what is not)

## Optional

- [FactLot Bench](https://github.com/9mp96ygnbk-alt/factlot/blob/main/bench/README.md): 14 CRE agent tasks with independently computed answers (not yet run on current models)
